--------
In this unreleased full interview from June 2018, Dallas rapper Yella Beezy joins VladTV for a detailed conversation about breaking out of a city not traditionally known for street rap stars. He explains how “That’s On Me,” “Up One” with Lil Baby, and “Traffic” grew from mixtape cuts and club records into major YouTube hits, while reflecting on Quality Control, Migos, Coach K, Drake, Gucci Mane, and Atlanta’s influence. Beezy also opens up about his Oak Cliff upbringing, losing his father in an unsolved cold case, teenage arrests in Texas, and using music to leave the streets behind. The interview covers Dallas hip hop history—from Erykah Badu and Post Malone to Vanilla Ice—plus DJ Screw, Pimp C, lean culture, kidney stones, jewelry, trucking investments, and his upcoming first album. A candid look at ambition, survival, and putting Dallas on the rap map.

--------
In this VladTV interview, Marlow Bates reflects on the height of Baltimore’s drug era, the police investigation he says targeted him, and alleged encounters with Edward Burns, the former detective who later co-created HBO’s The Wire. Bates claims he served 37 years for a crime he did not commit and describes how crews moved money and product between Baltimore and New York, sometimes earning tens of thousands a day.

He also opens up about the reality behind the headline: before prison, he says he knew of roughly $5 million in cash waiting for him — only to learn after decades behind bars that the money was gone. Now, Bates says he is “broke” and warns younger people not to chase street life, jewelry, cars, or quick money, urging them to invest in legitimate business instead.

DJ Vlad sits down with Terrance “Gangsta” Williams to unpack the public fallout with Boosie Badazz, from interview payments and VladTV membership claims to Boosie’s alleged $600,000 business dispute now headed through court. The conversation turns to the police report behind the snitching debate, with Vlad and Williams discussing accusations that Boosie pointed to his security guard over an illegal gun found during a traffic stop and allegedly pressured him to take the charge. Williams explains why he sees it as cooperating, while referencing Wack 100, Mississippi controversy, Roland Martin, and the street-code backlash surrounding the case. Vlad also addresses Boosie’s failed paywall interview strategy, Patreon talk, their possible future business relationship, and comments about gambling at home, tying it to Gilbert Arenas’ federal case. A candid look at hip-hop media, loyalty, paperwork, and online feuds.

--------
Charleston White joins VladTV to react to reports surrounding Sean “Diddy” Combs’ alleged prison fight, rumored transfer, and claims involving a Shower Posse figure, a cell phone sweep, and a hospital visit outside the facility. Vlad breaks down how attention around Diddy’s alleged privileges may have led to prison officials searching cells, while Charleston questions why punishments and transfers followed if “nothing happened.” The conversation turns to whether Diddy will be embraced when he comes home, with Charleston arguing that despite bumps and bruises behind bars, Diddy’s reputation may remain strong because he hasn’t publicly complained and still carries cultural influence. He also criticizes Black media outlets and personalities for staying largely silent throughout Diddy’s legal troubles, calling silence a form of agreement. A candid discussion on prison politics, celebrity status, accountability, and how hip-hop culture responds when powerful figures face scandal.

--------
Tito “TJ” Dominguez sits down with Vlad to recount the surreal excess and danger of the 1980s drug era, from running a Lamborghini dealership and overnighting a car to the King of Saudi Arabia by chartered jumbo jet, to flying Concorde between New York, Europe, Zurich, Heathrow, and Charles de Gaulle. He recalls lavish days at The Palace, encounters with Leona Helmsley, and a lifestyle fueled by millions.

The conversation turns to Colombia, Carlos Lehder’s 1987 extradition to the United States, and Pablo Escobar’s violent campaign against extradition. Dominguez explains how Escobar’s decision to put bounties on police officers pushed Colombia toward crisis, with young people killing cops for cash and law enforcement forced out of uniform. He reflects on law and order, his own sons in policing, and why Escobar’s war on police helped change the country’s extradition battle.

--------
John Franzese Jr. sits down with VladTV to revisit growing up under the shadow of the Colombo crime family after his father faced a 50-year prison sentence. He recalls how his brother Michael Franzese became increasingly close to their father’s associates and was later made in the family, explaining the Mafia structure, captains, Andrew Russo, and what it meant to be a “good fellow.” Franzese also shares a vivid childhood memory from school, where a classmate brought newspaper stories about his father into current events, prompting his mother to confront the teacher. From Mineola’s Body Shop to a Chinese restaurant near Hillside and Herrick Road, this interview offers a personal look at family, stigma, organized crime, and the realities behind the headlines surrounding John “Sonny” Franzese, Michael Franzese, the Teamsters, and New York Mafia history.
